brief: A wall clock with hands that turn and tell the time.

requirements.requirement: Wall clock with hands that turn and tell the time
requirements.evidence: No clock mechanism parts exist in Hex Cluster catalog (find_parts clock/dial/hand returned no clock parts). Build is a single hex base with top cover (cover:0,0,0;full;top) and wall keyhole accessory for wall mounting; pencil prop on top loosely represents clock hands positionally but does not turn, has no movement, numerals, or timekeeping. Configurator checks fit only, no timekeeping function.

finish.summary: Single-cell wall-mountable base with cover prepared for clock face staging; true turning clock hands and time-telling not possible with available 3D-printed static parts - only a pencil pose suggests hand positions. check_build OK, meshClash clear.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
